ask: C11, no dependencies. lines.c: Bresenham line drawing with Cohen-Sutherland clipping to a viewport, midpoint circle and filled circle, an 8-bit framebuffer struct with putpixel bounds checks, and a PGM dump. main draws a clipped test pattern. write the file.
prose:
The file wrote cleanly. Build and run:

```sh
cc -std=c11 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -o lines lines.c -lm
./lines > out.pgm
```

Open `out.pgm` with any image viewer that handles PGM (Preview, feh, GIMP, `eog`). What you'll see: a dark-gray 512×512 canvas, a 40 px inset viewport border, a 36-ray starburst clipped hard at the viewport edges, a hatched diagonal grid also clipped, three concentric circles (outline), four filled blobs at the compass points on the outer ring, a dark filled centre circle, and the two full-frame diagonals underneath everything.

The `-lm` flag is the only external dependency — `cos`/`sin` from `<math.h>` for the starburst angles. Everything else (Bresenham, Cohen-Sutherland, midpoint circle, scanline fill, PGM write) is straight C11.
